input_signals.name: Debt-Light EBITDA Strength
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA profitability should command a stronger return premium when it is supported by low financial debt intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This uses a continuous debt-burden interaction rather than a hard deleveraging gate, avoiding a degenerate zero-valued short leg. The signal favors firms that combine sustained operating profitability with financial health, distinguishing unlevered operating strength from EBITDA generated under heavy debt dependence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( ebitda, at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Backed Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(act, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability is more valuable when near-term liquidity comfortably covers current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: A smoothed oibdp/assets leg favors firms with persistent operating yield rather than a one-period spike. The current-asset-to-current-liability quality leg rewards firms less exposed to refinancing or working-capital stress, making high profitability more likely to persist.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deficit Profit Rebound Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability rebounds at firms with accumulated retained-earnings deficits are less reliable and should predict weaker future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: A sharp improvement in operating profitability can look attractive, but when it occurs at a firm with a weak cumulative earnings history it may represent a transient turnaround rather than durable strength. The signal is high specifically for the combination of improving operating profit and poor retained-earnings quality, so the expected return slope should be negative.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Internally Funded RND Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))), RANK(RATIO(re, ADD(ABS(re), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-adjusted operating profitability is more valuable when it is supported by internally accumulated earnings rather than a weak claims structure.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding back R&D treats unreported R&D as zero and recognizes that some durable profitability is masked by expensed intangible investment. The retained-earnings-to-claims leg distinguishes self-financed compounders from firms whose apparent operating strength is less financially seasoned.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( re, add( abs( re ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Residual Cash Conversion Margin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), sale))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, oibdp), ADD(ABS(oibdp), lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margin is more durable when cash generation exceeds what would be mechanically implied by operating EBITDA, after accounting for near-term claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids double-counting oibdp by using residual cash conversion, SUB(oancf, oibdp), rather than raw operating cash flow. The quality leg asks whether cash conversion is strong relative to operating scale and current liabilities, so the interaction targets margin strength that is actually converting into financially usable cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), sale ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( oancf, oibdp ), add( abs( oibdp ), lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Efficient Margin Expansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 5)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(act, sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Margin expansion should predict higher returns when it is achieved without rising current-asset intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the accrual-heavy profit-spike template and tests a different mechanism: whether improving margins are supported by efficient working-capital use. If operating margins rise while current assets required per dollar of sales fall, the improvement is more likely to reflect scalable operating strength rather than inventory or receivables buildup.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( act, sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Capital Structure Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained EBITDA profitability should be more persistent when the firm’s funded-debt intensity is stable through time.
input_signals.reasoning: This differs from low-debt composites by focusing on capital-structure stability rather than debt level. High profitability paired with volatile debt intensity may reflect recapitalizations, financing stress, or episodic balance-sheet support, whereas stable debt intensity makes operating strength easier to underwrite.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( ebitda, at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid Profitability Floor
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(act, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating profitability has maintained a strong downside floor should earn higher returns when that persistence is paired with adequate short-term liquidity.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the residual cash-conversion leg with a direct persistence test: the profitability score is high only when recent worst-case oibdp/assets remains strong. Pairing that downside profit floor with act/lct targets durable operating strength that is less likely to be interrupted by liquidity pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maintenance-Stable EBITDA Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ebitda, at))), RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(dp, sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(lct, sale), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High EBITDA profitability is more durable when depreciation intensity and current-claim intensity are stable through time.
input_signals.reasoning: This reframes the maintenance issue as stability rather than penalizing depreciation levels inside a profit-scaled denominator. The quality leg is not mechanically decreasing in profitability; it discounts firms whose EBITDA may be less reliable because asset-consumption charges or short-term obligations are unstable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( ebitda, at ) ) ), rank( neg( sumrank( vol( ratio( dp, sale ), 5 ), vol( ratio( lct, sale ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid Sustained RND Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))), MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(RATIO(act, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-adjusted operating profitability is most valuable when the firm continues investing in R&D and maintains enough liquidity to support that investment.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding back R&D recognizes that expensed intangible investment can depress current operating profit even when it builds durable capability. The conditioning leg requires both sustained R&D commitment and current-liability coverage, separating self-reinforcing intangible profitability from temporary profit boosted by investment cuts or liquidity pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), min( rank( trend( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid Net Operating Floor
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(act, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A strong downside floor in operating profitability after interest expense is more valuable when the firm also has solid current-liability coverage.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the weak lct/sale stress leg with a liquidity cushion that has clearer financial-health content. The profitability leg is not the same raw oibdp floor; it tests whether operating profits remain positive after interest claims, then rewards that resilience only when short-term solvency is adequate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Trough EBITDA Debt Ceiling
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ebitda, at), 5)), RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A persistent EBITDA profitability floor should predict higher returns when the firm has not recently carried high funded-debt intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the signed-ratio pathology by using a monotone rank interaction: higher trough EBITDA raises the score, while higher recent peak debt always lowers it. The signal stress-tests both sides, favoring firms whose profitability survives bad periods and whose balance sheet has not depended on large funded-debt exposure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( ebitda, at ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( ts_max( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Backed Smooth Operating Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(act, lct)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profitability is more durable when its smoothed level is high relative to its own volatility and the firm maintains adequate liquidity.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the nearly saturated positive-profit count with a continuous profitability-minus-instability measure. It also avoids relying on current-liability volatility, which has shown weak portfolio evidence, and instead conditions smooth profitability on a clearer short-term financial-health measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ), vol( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Validated Margin Expansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 5)), MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, sale), 5)), RANK(RATIO(act, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-margin improvement should predict higher returns when cash-flow margin is also improving and liquidity remains sound.
input_signals.reasoning: This revises the margin-trend idea away from falling current liabilities, which can conflict with accrual-quality logic. It requires margin expansion to be validated by operating cash-flow improvement and a current-ratio cushion, making the signal less likely to reward accrual-driven or liquidity-stressed profit growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 5 ) ), min( rank( trend( ratio( oancf, sale ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid EBITDA Conversion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ebitda, at))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ABS(ebitda), dp))), RANK(RATIO(act, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA profitability is more valuable when it converts into operating income after depreciation and the firm has adequate liquidity.
input_signals.reasoning: This addresses the risk that high EBITDA overstates durable profitability for firms with large depreciation add-backs. The conversion leg rewards EBITDA that survives depreciation charges, while the liquidity leg reduces exposure to firms whose reported operating strength is vulnerable to current-claim pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( ebitda, at ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( abs( ebitda ), dp ) ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Ceiling Net Profit Momentum
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving operating profitability after interest should predict higher returns when the firm has not recently carried high funded-debt intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: Profit improvement is more credible when it remains visible after interest expense rather than being offset by financing costs. Conditioning on the recent maximum debt burden focuses on balance-sheet claim risk without using debt issuance changes, helping separate durable operating momentum from levered profit recoveries.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( ts_max( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded RND Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))), RANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-adjusted operating profitability is more durable when operating cash flow can fund both recent R&D commitments and current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the near-binary R&D reporting count with a continuous self-funding measure. The quality leg asks whether cash generation is sufficient relative to cumulative intangible investment and short-term claims, rather than simply restricting the signal to R&D reporters.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquid Gross Operating Conversion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ABS(SUB(revt, cogs)), xsga))), RANK(RATIO(act, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High gross profitability is more durable when it converts through overhead into operating income and is backed by adequate liquidity.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross profit can overstate operating strength if SG&A absorbs the surplus or if the firm lacks short-term financial flexibility. This signal rewards firms with strong gross economics only when those economics survive overhead costs and are paired with current-liability coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( abs( sub( revt, cogs ) ), xsga ) ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Interest Burden Stable Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(xint, ADD(ABS(oibdp), lct)), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability is more durable when the interest burden is stable relative to operating scale and near-term claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the debt-ceiling recombination with a fixed-charge stability mechanism rather than a debt-level signal. High operating profitability should be more valuable when interest expense does not fluctuate sharply relative to the firm’s operating cash-generating base and current-liability pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( xint, add( abs( oibdp ), lct ) ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Interest-Stable Gross Converter
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ABS(SUB(revt, cogs)), xsga))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(xint, ADD(ABS(oibdp), lct)), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability is more durable when it converts through SG&A into operating income and the firm’s interest burden is stable.
input_signals.reasoning: The conversion leg tests whether gross economics remain after operating overhead, while the quality leg focuses on fixed-charge stability rather than debt levels or current-ratio liquidity. Stable interest burden should help distinguish repeatable operating profitability from profit streams exposed to refinancing or rate shocks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( abs( sub( revt, cogs ) ), xsga ) ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( xint, add( abs( oibdp ), lct ) ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Demand-Stable Liquid Margin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oiadp, sale))), MIN(RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(sale, at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(act, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating margins are more valuable when the underlying sales base is stable and short-term liquidity is sound.
input_signals.reasoning: High margins can be cyclical or temporarily boosted if revenue is unstable. Conditioning on low sales-intensity volatility and a current-liability cushion targets firms with both durable demand and financial flexibility.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ) ), min( rank( neg( vol( ratio( sale, at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Covered Overhead Gross Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))), RANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(xsga, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability should be rewarded when operating cash flow can fund both overhead commitments and current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross profit is less valuable if the firm cannot convert operations into cash sufficient to cover SG&A needs and near-term claims. This signal targets firms whose product-level profitability is financially usable, not merely high before overhead and working-capital pressures.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, add( xsga, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net Overhead Interest Gross Converter
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), xint), ADD(ADD(ABS(SUB(revt, cogs)), xsga), lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability should predict higher returns when the gross surplus survives both overhead and interest costs while remaining large relative to current claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly fixes the missing-overhead critique by requiring gross profit to convert after SG&A and interest expense, rather than just swapping liquidity denominators. It also avoids reusing the act/lct conditioner, making the quality test about claim-adjusted conversion of gross economics into equity-relevant operating surplus.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), xint ), add( add( abs( sub( revt, cogs ) ), xsga ), lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover-Mix Stable Net Operating Yield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(dlc, lct), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability after interest expense is more durable when the short-term debt share of current liabilities is stable.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from low-debt intensity and instead tests rollover-composition stability: firms are not rewarded merely for having little debt. High after-interest operating profitability should be more reliable when current obligations are not being repeatedly reshuffled toward or away from short-term interest-bearing debt.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( dlc, lct ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Float Funded Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), lt), RATIO(dltt, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability is more durable when liabilities are tilted toward non-debt operating float rather than long-term funded debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This reinterprets the poor maturity-mix evidence by separating current operating liabilities from interest-bearing debt. Profitable firms with supplier/accrual float and less long-term funded debt may have scalable operating economics, whereas similar profits backed by funded leverage are less equity-resilient.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), lt ), ratio( dltt, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Float Gross Converter
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ABS(SUB(revt, cogs)), xsga))), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), lt), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), lt)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability is most valuable when it converts through overhead into operating income and the liability structure reflects operating float rather than funded debt.
input_signals.reasoning: The first two components preserve the strong gross-to-operating conversion mechanism, while the quality leg replaces generic liquidity or leverage with a liability-mix decomposition. It favors firms whose profitability is supported by routine operating liabilities and penalizes firms where funded debt dominates the claims structure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ind_adj( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ), min( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( abs( sub( revt, cogs ) ), xsga ) ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), lt ), ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), lt ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover-Stable Net Profit Floor
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, xint), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(VOL(SUB(RATIO(dlc, lct), RATIO(dltt, lt)), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A downside floor in operating profitability after interest expense is more valuable when the firm’s debt maturity mix is stable.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids reusing interest-expense volatility as the conditioner and instead tests whether financing structure is being reshuffled between short-term and long-term debt. Stable rollover composition should make an after-interest profit floor more durable and less exposed to refinancing-driven reversals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( vol( sub( ratio( dlc, lct ), ratio( dltt, lt ) ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Margin Floor Operating Float
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), 5)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), lt), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent industry-adjusted operating margins should predict higher returns when liabilities are tilted toward non-debt operating float rather than funded debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This restores industry comparability for the operating-margin floor and replaces the weak demand-volatility recombination with a liability-mix mechanism. The quality leg rewards firms funded more by routine operating liabilities and less by debt claims, helping separate scalable operating profitability from levered profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ind_adj( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), 5 ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), lt ), ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RND Adjusted Overhead Converter
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ADD(ABS(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), ABS(SUB(xsga, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-adjusted operating profitability is more durable when it converts into R&D-adjusted operating income after non-R&D overhead and current claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the weak retained-capital-minus-current-claims leg and handles R&D consistently by adding it back to profitability while excluding it from the overhead burden. Treating unreported R&D as zero is economically justified, and the conversion leg tests whether intangible-adjusted profitability survives non-R&D SG&A and near-term liability pressure.
